messages:
maria (runtime): uploaded an nsys trace for the 3/10 regression — median latency up ~18% on long-seq runs. link: https://files.redwood.dev/traces/1865432100-hostcopy.nsys

noah (perf): grabbing it now. quick q: was this collected with streaming enabled and pinned host memory?

maria (runtime): yes, nsys cmd was: 
```
nsys profile -o hostcopy_reg --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=cpu -t none --capture-range=nvtx --chop  --force-overwrite ./run_infer.sh --seq-len 2048
```
we used cudaHostAlloc (pinned) for prefetch buffers.

rafi (infra): timeline looks weird — long idle on CPU between memcpy bursts. I see big memcpy H2D on stream 4, then ~60ms CPU gap, then kernel on stream 0. Are memcpy batches happening on the main thread?

maria (runtime): yes, prefetch loop is single-threaded currently. The prefetcher issues a sequence of cudaMemcpyAsync for each KV chunk then synchronizes with an event before scheduling the compute batch. suspected cause: host thread yields and gets preempted between issuing the last memcpy and the compute launch.

noah (perf): I see two things in the nsys timeline: 1) memcpy operations are not overlapping with kernels as much as expected (streams not parallelized). 2) some memcpy operations are falling back to pageable path (stacked H2D markers with high CPU time). Could be because we hit non-pinned path for some buffers (maybe registration dropped).

maria (runtime): good catch. I confirm cudaHostAlloc flags were set but registration is conditional on buffer lifecycle; we might be reusing buffers across requests in a way that unregisters them. Also the memcpy sizes are tiny (~32KB) which kills throughput.

noah (perf): suggestions: 1) coalesce small prefetch copies into a single larger async copy per request (reduce syscall/driver overhead). 2) move submit path off the hot worker thread — use a short bounded thread pool to batch and issue memcpys so we avoid a single-thread preemption hole. 3) verify all buffers are pinned at the point of memcpy (add an assert around cudaHostGetDevicePointer).

rafi (infra): from a scheduling standpoint, also consider assigning stream priorities and using a dedicated copy engine stream (if HW supports) so kernels on high-priority compute streams don't wait for copy submission ordering. I can roll out a small test on our perf nodes to try stream priorities + cudaMemcpyAsync flags.

maria (runtime): initial micropatch pushed to branch: runtime/hostcopy-coalesce. Changes: coalesce adjacent 32KB copies into 1x512KB chunk, move io submit to helper thread, add NVTX around submit. Patch reduces number of memcpy events by ~7x in my local nsys run and removes the CPU gap. link to patch: https://git.redwood.dev/runtime/compare/hostcopy-coalesce

perf-bot: nightly-run summary for branch hostcopy-coalesce: median latency on long-seq (2048) down 12% vs main, p95 down 9%. Full artifacts: https://ci.redwood.dev/artifacts/1865432100

noah (perf): nice. two follow-ups: 1) add a small assert to fail fast when a memcpy returns fallback (log cudaErrorInvalidValue or driver fallback). 2) benchmark pinned vs reg-locked behavior over prolonged reuse. We should also add a perf test that simulates OS preemption (stress with linux 'stress-ng --cpu 2') to ensure thread offloading is robust.

maria (runtime): will do. I'll also instrument NVTX ranges for: prefetch-issue, prefetch-complete, compute-launch so we can correlate in perf dashboards. Next steps: land coalesce PR behind a runtime flag, run dedicated perf sweep on prod-like nodes, then enable by default if stable.

rafi (infra): I'll run the stream-priority experiment on the perf pool tomorrow and report numbers. If we see further improvement, we can combine both fixes (coalescing + priority).

noah (perf): thumbs up. if anyone hits an outlier after landing, post another timeline and include the raw cudaMemcpy sizes (I want to ensure we didn't accidentally create a super-large copy for tiny requests). :thumbsup:
